title: Yara and the Colony Revisited
premise: Ada Sandoval smuggles memories in sealed neural wafers along the silent corridor between the warring colonies of Meridian and Vesper, keeping his head down and his past erased. When a manifest lists a ship that never flew and a name he doesn't recognize — Yara — he discovers the message he's carrying is a peace treaty encoded in a dead woman's memories, and that both governments will kill to own or destroy it. Hunted by customs enforcers, Vesperian agents, and the ghost of his own deleted identity, Ada must choose between delivering the message and protecting the people who helped him carry it. In the end he broadcasts the treaty from inside the jump gate itself, ending the war at the cost of his anonymity — and learns that Yara was the self he erased, coming home.
about_author: Ivo Ishikawa is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing shipping manifests before turning them into fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable gravity and write about the people who move between worlds.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Ada runs contraband memory-wafers through orbital customs on the freighter Pale Meridian, narrating his careful invisibility. POV: Ada. Beat: competent calm masking deep loneliness; establishes the silent war between Meridian and Vesper.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghost
chapters.summary: Customs clerk Oyelaran flags an anomaly: a ship that never flew appears on Ada's route history, carrying one passenger named Yara Sandoval. POV: Ada. Beat: unease — the name feels like a word on the tip of his tongue.

chapters.title: Wafer Work
chapters.summary: In his cramped cargo bay, Ada inspects his latest shipment and finds one wafer sealed with government-grade encryption he's never seen. POV: Ada. Beat: curiosity overriding professional caution; he almost plugs it in.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Oyelaran detains Ada for a routine scan, probing about the phantom ship. POV: Oyelaran. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; she's not corrupt, just honest, which is more dangerous.

chapters.title: Yara
chapters.summary: Alone, Ada jacks the encrypted wafer and experiences fragments: a woman's life, a laboratory, his own face younger. POV: Ada. Beat: vertigo of recognition — the memories are his, from a self he paid to have deleted.

chapters.title: Meridian Station Blues
chapters.summary: Ada hides at a waystation bar run by ex-smuggler Doss, asking about pre-war Meridian research stations. POV: Ada. Beat: reluctant alliance; Doss recognizes the wafer's lab markings and goes quiet with fear.

chapters.title: Vesperian Contact
chapters.summary: A Vesperian agent, Corvane, offers Ada triple rate to hand over 'the Yara consignment,' revealing both sides know it exists. POV: Ada. Beat: the trap closes — refusing means suspicion, accepting means complicity.

chapters.title: What the War Ate
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: the colony war's origins, told through station gossip and newsreels Ada half-remembers. POV: Ada. Beat: melancholy worldbuilding; two worlds that speak only through smugglers like him.

chapters.title: Doss's Price
chapters.summary: Doss agrees to forge transit papers but demands Ada tell him what's in the wafer. Ada shows him a fragment; Doss goes pale — he knew Yara. POV: Doss. Beat: grief surfacing; the past has witnesses after all.

chapters.title: Run the Gap
chapters.summary: A customs interdiction forces Ada to fly the Pale Meridian through an uncharted debris field. POV: Ada. Beat: white-knuckle action; he survives on instinct older than his memory.

chapters.title: Second Self
chapters.summary: Ada probes deeper into the wafer: Yara was a researcher who discovered the war's true cause — a manufactured incident both governments used to seize power. POV: Ada/Yara interleaved. Beat: revelation reframes everything; the war is a lie.

chapters.title: Corvane's Patience
chapters.summary: Corvane boards under diplomatic flag, courteous and lethal, making clear Vesper will burn the Pale Meridian rather than let the message jump. POV: Corvane. Beat: chilling charm; the antagonist believes he's the reasonable one.

chapters.title: Oyelaran's Choice
chapters.summary: Oyelaran finds Ada again, off-duty and off-record, and admits she traced the phantom ship too — her sister died in the manufactured incident. POV: Oyelaran. Beat: unexpected allyship born of shared loss.

chapters.title: The Message Itself
chapters.summary: Fully decoded, the wafer contains not just evidence but a negotiated ceasefire framework Yara built with defectors on both sides before her death. POV: Ada. Beat: awe and terror — he's carrying a peace that must reach living hands.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Gone Wrong
chapters.summary: Ada attempts to pass the wafer to a Meridian dissident cell; the meet is compromised by a double agent. POV: Ada. Beat: betrayal and escape; trust becomes a currency he can't afford.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Both governments flag the Pale Meridian; every port denies docking. Ada is now officially a ghost aboard a ghost ship. POV: Ada. Beat: isolation tightening; the long route is closing behind him.

chapters.title: Doss's Debt
chapters.summary: Doss reveals he sold information years ago that helped trigger the incident Yara exposed — and wants redemption. POV: Doss. Beat: guilt made useful; an old man betting his last years on one delivery.

chapters.title: Jump Window
chapters.summary: The only viable jump window to neutral relay Station Anvil opens in eleven days; after that, the corridor seals for a season. POV: Ada. Beat: clock starts ticking; structure tightens around the deadline.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer, Revised
chapters.summary: Corvane offers Ada immunity and a new identity if he surrenders the wafer — echoing the deal that erased Yara. POV: Ada. Beat: temptation as mirror; he sees how his old self was bought.

chapters.title: Who Was Yara
chapters.summary: Through the wafer, Ada lives Yara's final weeks: her love affair, her doubts, her decision to encode herself into the message. POV: Yara. Beat: intimate elegy; Ada grieves someone who is also himself.

chapters.title: The Erasure Clinic
chapters.summary: Ada tracks the clinic that deleted his memory, finding its proprietor kept backups — including the contract naming who paid for the erasure: Meridian intelligence. POV: Ada. Beat: horror of purchased forgetting; his whole life was someone's cleanup operation.

chapters.title: Stowaway
chapters.summary: Oyelaran defects, smuggling herself aboard the Pale Meridian with customs codes that can open closed ports. POV: Oyelaran. Beat: hope with teeth; the crew of ghosts grows.

chapters.title: Ambush at Relay Nine
chapters.summary: Vesper gunships trap the Pale Meridian at a relay; Doss takes the conn and flies a suicidal slingshot that saves the ship but wrecks the drive. POV: Doss. Beat: heroic sacrifice; the old man buys them time with his ship.

chapters.title: Drifting
chapters.summary: Crippled and dark, the ship coasts toward Anvil on residual momentum while Ada and Oyelaran repair what they can. POV: alternating. Beat: quiet dread and growing intimacy between the two survivors.

chapters.title: Confessions in the Dark
chapters.summary: With nothing but time, Ada tells Oyelaran about Yara; Oyelaran tells him about her sister. Two griefs recognize each other. POV: alternating. Beat: tenderness against duty — the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Anvil
chapters.summary: They limp into neutral Station Anvil, where the treaty's surviving drafters are rumored to live in exile. POV: Ada. Beat: cautious arrival; the message may finally find hands.

chapters.title: The Exiles
chapters.summary: Ada meets the exile circle led by former Meridian negotiator Hesh, who confirms the treaty framework but says it needs broadcast on both homeworlds' public bands to take root. POV: Ada. Beat: the plan crystallizes — and its impossibility with it.

chapters.title: Corvane Arrives
chapters.summary: Corvane reaches Anvil with warrants and bribes; the station's neutrality begins cracking under pressure. POV: Corvane. Beat: siege politics; even neutral ground bends to power.

chapters.title: Hesh's Doubt
chapters.summary: Hesh hesitates: broadcasting could reignite the war if either government spins it first. He wants to wait for a better moment. POV: Hesh. Beat: institutional caution versus desperate urgency; duty argues with itself.

chapters.title: Theft
chapters.summary: The wafer is stolen from Anvil's vault — Corvane's agents, aided by a traitor among the exiles. POV: Ada. Beat: lowest point; everything lost with four days left in the window.

chapters.title: Traitor's Face
chapters.summary: Ada identifies the exile traitor and confronts him: a man who lost everything in the war and believes peace is a fantasy. POV: Ada. Beat: anger tempered by understanding; corruption explained, not excused.

chapters.title: Recovery Run
chapters.summary: Ada and Oyelaran infiltrate Corvane's docked frigate to retake the wafer. POV: alternating. Beat: tense heist; they succeed but Corvane lets them — a trap within the trap.

chapters.title: Corvane's Truth
chapters.summary: Cornered, Corvane admits the war sustains both regimes' power — and that he'd rather die than preside over its end. POV: Corvane. Beat: the antagonist fully articulated; ideology as armor.

chapters.title: Two Days
chapters.summary: With the window closing, Hesh finally commits: the exiles will back the broadcast. The plan targets the jump gate's relay array itself. POV: Ada. Beat: resolve hardening; no more half-measures.

chapters.title: Boarding the Gate
chapters.summary: The repaired-enough Pale Meridian makes for the jump gate, flying straight through a Meridian blockade using Oyelaran's stolen codes. POV: Oyelaran. Beat: audacious gambit; her betrayal of her old institution completed.

chapters.title: Corvane's Last Intercept
chapters.summary: Corvane rams the gate approach; Ada transfers to the relay core via EVA while Doss's autopilot sacrifices the ship as cover. POV: Ada. Beat: climax begins; everything risked on one spacewalk.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Inside the gate array, Ada jacks the wafer directly into the system: Yara's memories, the evidence, and the treaty flood every public band in both systems simultaneously. POV: Ada. Beat: cathartic climax; the truth cannot be un-heard.

chapters.title: What Power Does
chapters.summary: Corvane dies refusing to stand down; Meridian and Vesper fleets hold fire as their populations erupt in protest and demand. POV: multiple brief vignettes. Beat: the war ends not with victory but with exposure.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the corridor reopens with traffic between reconciled worlds. Ada, publicly known now, chooses to keep smuggling — legally, carrying messages families exchange across the new peace. POV: Ada. Beat: bittersweet resolution; visibility accepted, purpose found.

chapters.title: Yara and the Colony Revisited
chapters.summary: Ada visits Yara's memorial on Meridian and speaks aloud to the self he erased, finally integrating her memories instead of fearing them. POV: Ada. Beat: quiet coda; identity restored not as recovery but as choice — he carries her forward willingly.
